title: Research sprint goal: Orchestration features: ops rows, goal clause map, rescope, query log apply
goal: Answer the sprint goal's questions that the public pack covers weakly, with the kb tools first and the live docs for gaps: Q1 which operational rows (land.end, land.step, done.refused, agent.run) the query log stores per item; Q2 how backlog.py precheck splits a sprint goal into clauses; Q5 how query log apply chooses the lead passage for a rules finding. Q3 (who may change a sprint's goal with backlog.py set) and Q4 (how close --summary maps goal clauses to items) are good. All five are about the kb's own tools, which kb/_self answers (pack --root _self cites its passages), so the finding is expected to end with a No outside facts: note.
notes:
Planned 2026-10-10: public pack coverage Q1 weak, Q2 weak, Q3 good, Q4 good, Q5 weak; pack --root _self answers all five.
Finding 2026-10-10 (rag.py pack --root _self, then the code each doc names). Q1: four closed ops events per item in the ops sidecar (kb/_self/querylog.md:53,102): land.step (item, step, exit, ms), land.end (item, exit, ms, lane), done.refused (item, reasons, ms; checks), agent.run (group, ms; agent, item only for a work/<id> branch). Q2: precheck SP does not split a goal: it runs the open items' checks once and warns of one that passes (kb/_self/tools.md:82); the only split is close --summary's, at '; ' and ', and ', a list clause further at ', ' and ' and ' (tools.md:84, backlog.md:242; bl_land.py:2150); precheck naming clauses is in-flight ST-ylje2dxh. Q3: nobody today: set refuses --goal on a sprint (bl_items.py:484, exit 2) and on a done item; the docs (tools.md:75, backlog.md:30) omit the sprint refusal; ST-ifljijni makes it operator only (--by operator). Q4: close --summary names each clause with the sprint's done item whose title and goal hold half its words, else its parts, else 'unmet' (backlog.md:242). Q5: a weak finding with no answer line and no key_missing takes the first pack --root _self passage (ql_apply.lead_passage) as its answer, gets an anchor phrase and the eval-row gates; the row stays only if they hold, else no-fix (querylog.md:169).
No outside facts: all five questions are about this kb's own tools, documented only by kb/_self and the code; no outside source covers them.
